root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `config_open_for_fuzzing()` hands the fuzz buffer to `config_init_data()`, the call length must stay strictly below the 32768-byte `static_data` capacity so the lexer keeps one in-bounds byte available for the EOF/backup path.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable program forwards the full copied extent `len` unchanged, so a 32768-byte fuzz input makes the lexer boundary land exactly at the right edge of `static_data`. The fixed program instead passes one fewer byte, restoring the missing in-bounds slack byte.

nodes.state: At EOF, `next()` stores `lexer->end + 1` into `lexer->pos`, creating the past-end lexer state that the subsequent `backup()` call consumes.
At the crash site, `backup()` dereferences `*lexer->pos` with `lexer->pos == lexer->end`, so the read lands exactly on the boundary that is one byte past `static_data` in the vulnerable run.

edges.relation: The fuzz harness forwards the clamped copied byte count unchanged from `size` into the fuzz-only `len` handoff.
The same call length handed off by `config_open_for_fuzzing()` becomes the `len` that materializes the lexer boundary in `config_init_data()`.
The boundary pointer created as `(char *)data + len` is the same `lexer->end` value that the EOF branch uses when it writes `lexer->pos = lexer->end + 1`.
The EOF boundary carried through `next()` is the same address that `backup()` later decrements to and dereferences as its sink pointer.
